subject: Error messages with ranef() and GOF tests on gdistremoval model

messages.author: 46c964e9fbebd352
messages.subject: Error messages with ranef() and GOF tests on gdistremoval model
parts:
Hello,
I have fit bird count data with gdistremoval(), following Ken's advice (thank you so much Ken Kellner!). But I am having trouble using ranef() and running GOF tests on the best-supported model, to see how well the model fits. The error I am getting with ranef() is:

> (re <- ranef(gdr_best_mod)) Error in out[, , t] <- cbind(means[, t], modes[, t], CI[, , t]) : incorrect number of subscripts

And when I try to assess model fit, I run into errors with these functions as well:

> residuals(gdr_best_mod) Error in det[, , t] <- dist[, , t] * phi[, rep(t, ncol(dist[, , t]))] : object of type 'closure' is not subsettable
> fitted(gdr_best_mod) Error in det[, , t] <- dist[, , t] * phi[, rep(t, ncol(dist[, , t]))] : object of type 'closure' is not subsettable Ho However, I have no difficulty with other functions such as predict(). 

Has anyone come across a similar issue? I'm wondering if I specified my model incorrectly, but except for these three functions everything has been running smoothly. For reference, my model is below:

> gdr_best_mod Call: gdistremoval(lambdaformula = ~yr_sc + hab_type_comb, phiformula = ~1, removalformula = ~1, distanceformula = ~hab_type + weather_wind_comb, data = umf_gdr, keyfun = "exp", output = "density", unitsOut = "ha", mixture = "P", K = starting_k * 4, starts = coef(gdr_best_mod_temp2), se = TRUE, control = list(maxit = 1e+05)) Abundance: Estimate SE z P(>|z|) (Intercept) 2.41 3.8662 0.622 0.53366 yr_sc -0.21 0.0651 -3.231 0.00124 hab_type_combnot_forest -1.26 0.5149 -2.442 0.01463 Availability: Estimate SE z P(>|z|) -1.43 4.79 -0.299 0.765 Distance: Estimate SE z P(>|z|) (Intercept) -3.501 0.0833 -42.045 0.0000 hab_typemixed 0.886 0.5814 1.525 0.1274 hab_typeopen 0.342 0.4425 0.773 0.4395 weather_wind_combwindy -1.063 0.3257 -3.264 0.0011 Removal: Estimate SE z P(>|z|) -0.464 0.125 -3.7 0.000216 AIC: 2032.963

I have used the same data with gdistsamp() and gmultmix()--that is, the yRemoval and yDistance matrices, siteCovs, and yearlySIteCovs used in the unmarked frame for gdistremoval() were also used in the unmarked frames for gdistsamp() and gmultmix() and I was able to use ranef() and run GOF tests on those models.

Any thoughts and suggestions would be much appreciated. Thank you so much!

Ellen

messages.author: 46c964e9fbebd352
messages.subject: Re: Error messages with ranef() and GOF tests on gdistremoval model
parts:
FOLLOW-UP with additional information....

I think I have a little sense of what might be going on with my gdistremoval() model. When I apply bup() to ranef(gdr_best_mod) and convert it to a dataframe, I am getting two columns of results. In my actual data, I have two visits per site-year (each row is a site-year, because the years are stacked in this dataset). I'm using the repeat visits to try to estimate phi due to temporary emigration. When I use these same data (two visits per site-year, to estimate TE) with gdistsamp() or gmultmix(), then ranef() on those models gives an estimated superpopulation size for each site-year. Therefore, I get one value per row of data.

Using ranef() on the gdistremoval() model gives two values per row of data. I don't think it is giving me a separate density estimate for each visit, because the first row of data (see below) is all zero's. And the second row of data has NA for site-years when there was only one visit (pre-2019, each site was visited once per year, so in the response matrices I have NA's for those missing surveys; but for the siteCovs and yearlySiteCovs I have non-NA placeholder values for those missing surveys).

> data.frame(bup(re, stat = "mean")) %>% head() X1 X2 1 0 NA 2 0 NA 3 0 NA 4 0 35.43442 5 0 32.70915 6 0 29.24418

Is it possible that in my response matrices (yDistance and yRemoval) are not allowed to have NA's for missing surveys? I didn't get an error message when I created the unmarked frame, so I thought that was okay.

I'm not quite sure what is going on with site-years for which there were two visits, though. Is the number in the second column (e.g., 35.43 in row 4 col 2 above) the estimated superpopulation size? Should I just ignore the first column that is all zero's?

Thanks for any ideas anyone may have on this.

Ellen

parts:
This seems to be a bug in one of the gdistremoval methods when there are multiple sampling periods. I think I know the issue but it would be helpful to examine the results from your actual model to confirm. Can you email me the top model off-list, as an Rds or Rdata file?

Thanks,

Ken
